nodes.label: Imported heightfield
nodes.description: Load a local grayscale PNG/TIFF or square little-endian R16. Explicit decoding preserves elevations. Sources are embedded in saved projects and exports.

nodes.label: Imported mask
nodes.description: Read a grayscale selection image. Integer samples map to 0–1; float samples are clamped. Range mode stretches the source minimum/maximum. Row zero is north.

nodes.label: Fractal noise
nodes.description: FastNoise Lite noise in world metres. Seed offset adds to the world seed.

nodes.label: Authored landforms
nodes.description: Existing ranges, peaks and basins from the recipe. Edit their coordinates in the project JSON.

nodes.label: Domain warp
nodes.description: Bend terrain coordinates with two coherent noise fields; amplitude is measured in metres.

nodes.label: Combine terrain
nodes.description: Blend two heightfields with 24 mathematical modes. Nonlinear modes use the reference elevation as 1.0; mix/add/subtract/min/max preserve metres. Separation identifies the top layer's contribution.

nodes.label: Smooth
nodes.description: Gaussian smoothing with a radius in world metres.

nodes.label: Terrace
nodes.description: Create strata at fixed height intervals. Softness rounds each step.

nodes.label: Remap elevation
nodes.description: Fit the incoming height range to a new range, with an optional curve.

nodes.label: Stream erosion
nodes.description: Stream-power incision and hillslope diffusion. Wear is removed height, normalized to a mask.

nodes.label: Thermal erosion
nodes.description: Move material down slopes above the talus angle. Closed edges conserve material; a mask blends the result.

nodes.label: Hydraulic erosion
nodes.description: Continuous droplet paths erode and transport sediment. Closed boundaries return all carried material; open boundaries report discharged load. Mask limits mobility; rainfall controls droplet origins. White resistance blocks erosion while still permitting deposition.

nodes.label: Height selector
nodes.description: Select a band of elevation with feathered edges. White includes, black excludes.

nodes.label: Slope selector
nodes.description: Select a slope band in degrees, measured at this graph's sampling resolution.

nodes.label: Radial falloff
nodes.description: A circular inclusion mask in world metres. Useful for islands and local operations.

nodes.label: Combine masks
nodes.description: Combine two selection masks, clamped to zero through one.

nodes.label: Invert mask
nodes.description: Swap included and excluded areas.

nodes.label: Terrain output
nodes.description: The height field used for builds. Water routing and paint maps run after this node.

nodes.label: Constant height
nodes.description: A flat elevation field in metres.

nodes.label: Linear gradient
nodes.description: A ramp with a world-space direction and elevation range.

nodes.label: Mountain
nodes.description: Place a mountain with a compact footprint. Natural starts with broad divides, rounded crests and limited fine-scale relief. Alpine and Massif retain their exaggerated profiles. Follow with Geologic weathering for channels and deposition.

nodes.label: Mountain range
nodes.description: A positioned, winding chain of peaks with controllable length, width and direction.

nodes.label: Drawn range
nodes.description: Draw a ridgeline in the layout view. Point coordinates are world metres; centre and rotation transform the path.

nodes.label: Canyon
nodes.description: An authored canyon path with a graded floor. Geologic walls add irregular alcoves, buttresses and sampling-aware strata. Layered preserves the original profile. Points run upstream to downstream.

nodes.label: Volcano
nodes.description: A placed volcanic cone with a caldera, radial ridges and an irregular rim.

nodes.label: Impact crater
nodes.description: An impact bowl with a raised rim, rough ejecta apron and optional central rebound.

nodes.label: Island
nodes.description: Draw a closed landmass outline. Coast breakup and inland ridges stay inside its feathered footprint.

nodes.label: Dune field
nodes.description: Wind-oriented asymmetrical dunes, with curved crests, spacing and relief controls.

nodes.label: Plateau
nodes.description: A positioned mesa with a broad top, broken escarpment and adjustable wall slope.

nodes.label: Transform
nodes.description: Translate, rotate and stretch a heightfield in world units. Outside pixels use the fill elevation.

nodes.label: River path
nodes.description: Graded preserves the original spline trench. Alluvial adds bounded bend migration, terrain confinement, pool cross sections and sediment-limited inner bars. It is a kinematic model, not 2D hydraulics. Guides pin the bankfull course; tributary joins and lake shores also pin the wet course. End at a world edge, lake or another river within Junction snap. Cutoffs and braiding are not simulated. In Alluvial, waterWidth(s) controls the channel; width and slot apply only to Graded.

waterWidths.label: Water widths at path points (m)
waterWidths.description: Empty uses uniform waterWidth. Otherwise provide one full width per control point; linear profile follows normalized control-point chord distance and survives clipping and reach splitting.

nodes.label: River network
nodes.description: Route drainage through the terrain and carve connected channels. Headwaters confines source regions while retaining their downstream flow.

nodes.label: Positioned lake
nodes.description: Choose a source inside a contained basin and an absolute water level. Exports coverage, depth and exterior shore masks. Authored water mode preserves enabled lake surfaces from this node's terrain; downstream transforms do not move them.

nodes.label: Lakes
nodes.description: Find enclosed depressions using priority-flood routing. Exposes lake coverage, depth and shore selections without inventing uphill water.

nodes.label: Shape mask
nodes.description: Place a circle, ellipse or box mask with feathered edges. White includes the selected area.

nodes.label: Layer stack
nodes.description: Seven ordered terrain layers, each with a blend mode, opacity and optional mask. Reorder layers in the inspector; unconnected layers are skipped.

nodes.label: Stratified rock
nodes.description: Uneven seeded layers with local folds, tilt and controllable ledges. Unresolved bands fade out on coarse grids. The ledges output selects flattened portions, not rock material types.

nodes.label: Clamp elevations
nodes.description: Limit terrain to a fixed elevation interval. Optional mask blends the clipped result.

nodes.label: Flip terrain
nodes.description: Mirror the heightfield across either world axis.

nodes.label: Median filter
nodes.description: Remove isolated spikes with a bounded median kernel. Radius is measured in world metres; the kernel is capped at 51 samples.

nodes.label: Sharpen terrain
nodes.description: Unsharp masking adds local relief relative to a smoothed surface.

nodes.label: Equalize heights
nodes.description: Redistribute the elevation histogram while preserving its endpoints. Blend strength controls contrast.

nodes.label: Profile curve
nodes.description: Shape elevation using five control values and monotone cubic interpolation between them. Input can be relative to the terrain or a fixed range.

nodes.label: Variable blur
nodes.description: A guide mask interpolates four Gaussian scales: black preserves detail, white applies the full radius.

nodes.label: Directional warp
nodes.description: A height guide displaces sampling along one direction. Guide elevation / reference controls signed displacement.

nodes.label: Slope warp
nodes.description: Move terrain sampling along the guide gradient. The displacement is bounded and measured in metres.

nodes.label: Expand / contract
nodes.description: A local maximum expands high ground; a local minimum contracts it. Uses a square footprint capped at 101 samples.

nodes.label: Distance mask
nodes.description: Distance to a mask boundary in world metres. Use the falloff outside a feature, or increasing distance inside it.

nodes.label: Curvature selector
nodes.description: Convex ridges and concave hollows from the Laplacian of a smoothed heightfield. This uses mean curvature response, not separate plan/profile modes.

nodes.label: Facing direction
nodes.description: Select slopes facing a compass angle: 0° is +X, 90° is +Y. Flat areas are excluded.

nodes.label: Peaks & ridges
nodes.description: Select positive relief above the local average. Radius sets the scale of ridges to include.

nodes.label: Fade borders
nodes.description: Bring height toward a chosen elevation along the world boundary.

nodes.label: Repeat terrain
nodes.description: Repeat an upstream tile across the domain. Use Seamless first to align opposite boundaries.

nodes.label: Match tile edges
nodes.description: Blend opposite borders to matching elevations for repeating tiles. Border values match; matching derivatives is not guaranteed.

nodes.label: Switch terrain
nodes.description: Choose one of two heightfields. Both branches are validated; cached evaluations are reused.

nodes.label: Compare heights
nodes.description: Compare two elevations with a tolerance and a soft transition. White marks the selected relation.

nodes.label: Fill depressions
nodes.description: Priority-flood depression filling with a minimum routing gradient. Changes terrain by raising pits, rather than cutting outlets.

nodes.label: Terrain palette
nodes.description: Map terrain elevation or an optional mask guide through an original five-color ramp. These are authored palettes, not satellite imagery.

nodes.label: Solid color
nodes.description: A uniform sRGB color for masked biome and surface layers.

nodes.label: Two-color tint
nodes.description: Map a mask between two sRGB colors. Input enhancement is explicit and off by default.

nodes.label: Blend colors
nodes.description: Blend two color layers through opacity and an optional mask. Linear-light mixing is the default; artistic sRGB blending is also available.

nodes.label: Adjust color
nodes.description: Hue rotation, saturation, lightness and gamma for sRGB colors. A mask limits adjustments; packed data is a separate type.

nodes.label: Pack RGB masks
nodes.description: Pack R/G/B masks as linear data. No gamma conversion. Each channel can optionally be enhanced; leave None for calibrated masks.

nodes.label: Unpack RGB masks
nodes.description: Recover the exact R/G/B masks from packed linear data. The average output is an arithmetic mean. Color textures are a distinct type.

nodes.label: Bedrock & alluvium
nodes.description: Stream power with alluvium (SPACE) transports loose sediment, erodes exposed bedrock and deposits material downstream. Optional soil creep and conversion share the same soil layer. White resistance protects bedrock, while existing soil remains mobile. A shared incision floor limits entrainment and creep without restoring removed material. Fixed outer heights with reported outlet sediment loss. Uncalibrated geological time, D8 routing.

flowArea.label: Flow mask reference (m² at unit runoff)

nodes.label: Soil & hillslope transport
nodes.description: Weather bedrock into mobile soil, then move only that soil downhill. Depth-dependent creep rounds soil-covered divides and fills hollows while bare resistant rock stays exposed. Closed, paired fluxes conserve volume. White resistance prevents rock conversion, not transport of existing soil; black mask protects both layers. Art-directed process, not calibrated geological time.

nodes.label: Geologic weathering
nodes.description: Carve broad valleys, then gullies and fine channels. Transfers only erosion/deposition changes back to the original surface, preserving existing fine detail. Optional native-resolution protection and rainfall masks; bounded total incision and conservative material accounting. CPU art-directed model, not calibrated geophysics.

nodes.label: Talus breakdown
nodes.description: Eight-neighbour slope transport with bedrock, seeded talus variation, directional bias and optional sediment loss. Mask blocks transport across protected cells. Wear/deposition masks use an explicit metre reference; diagnostics account for removed material.

nodes.label: Wind erosion
nodes.description: Directional surface abrasion and conservative airborne sediment advection. Exposed ground supplies material; sheltered ground settles it. Closed edges return carried load, open edges report export. This is a grid-based artistic model, not atmospheric CFD.

nodes.label: River channels
nodes.description: Carve rivers sized by their discharge: width w = a·Q^b and depth d = c·Q^f (Leopold & Maddock), with Q from the upstream area. Beds fall strictly downstream and only cut. Reaches meander on gentle slopes, braid where the slope is steep for the discharge, and run straight in steep or narrow valleys. Exports water depth, the wetted river, braid bars and channel width.

nodes.label: Erode (particles + sediment)
nodes.description: Rain drops run down the terrain, erode where they carry less than they could and settle where they carry more: channels and gullies cut in, fans, filled hollows and floodplains build up. Runs coarse to fine (valley-scale channels, then gully-scale rills); fresh sediment relaxes to its angle of repose. White resistance erodes no rock; rainfall scales the number of drops.

deathRadius.label: Spread of a stopped drop's load (m, 0 = at its cell)

grade.label: Floor grading of fresh sediment (0 = off)

nodes.label: Erosion detail
nodes.description: Carve branching, flow-aligned gullies into slopes without a simulation. Stripes run downhill and each finer octave follows the walls of the coarser gullies, so they branch like tributaries. No detail on flats or in channels; deeper in hollows, shallower on hard rock. Strata and joint sets act as resistance, not as added height. Gullies start only where enough area drains down a steep enough slope (channel heads), never point into closed depressions, and leave a ring around small lakes. Outputs the gully and ridge masks and the resistance used.

nodes.label: Floodplain and terraces
nodes.description: Flatten valley floors next to rivers into floodplains at the bankfull level, with natural levees and back-swamp wetlands, and cut river terraces above them. Everything is measured as height above the nearest channel (HAND) along the flow, so the shapes follow the drainage instead of absolute contours.

nodes.label: Flow routing
nodes.description: Analyse drainage without changing the terrain. Routes water with D8, random D8, multiple flow directions or D-infinity over filled, carved or basin-linked depressions, and exports flow, channels, height above drainage, wetness, lake depth, drainage basins and stream order. Every mask is scaled by an explicit area or height, not by its own maximum.

nodes.label: Geology (rock volume)
nodes.description: A 3D rock volume under the terrain: dipping, folded and faulted beds of hard and soft rock, with joint sets and fault damage zones. The terrain passes through carrying the rock, and Erode samples it at the eroding surface as it cuts down, so hard beds stand as ledges, ribs and benches and joints steer gullies. Resistance is the rock at the input surface (white = hard) for any node with a resistance input; bed and joints show the hardness and the weak zones, layers numbers the beds.

nodes.label: Glaciate
nodes.description: Carve the terrain with glaciers at their maximum extent: steady-state balance-flux ice above an equilibrium-line altitude, abrasion that scales with sliding speed (U-shaped troughs, hanging tributary valleys, overdeepenings), cirques with tarns at glacier heads, lateral and terminal moraines, then a post-glacial river pass. Physical units: metres and years. Large-scale work runs on an internal ice grid; fine detail outside the ice is kept.

elaFraction.label: ELA height in the relief (0 = lowest, 1 = highest)

nodes.label: Gullies (fine incision)
nodes.description: Cut real gullies at full resolution: water is routed locally, channels incise where enough area drains down a steep enough slope (the channel head sets the gully spacing, tens of metres), and hillslopes between them are rounded by soil creep that speeds up towards the critical slope while cliffs stay sharp. Gives the 8-64 m relief of real mountains instead of uniform noise. Runs tile by tile on big terrains. Optional resistance (hard rock incises and creeps less) and mask. Outputs the terrain, the channel mask and the incision depth.

nodes.label: Hydro fix
nodes.description: Make the terrain drain: cut outlets through the barriers of closed depressions (least-cost breaching), up to a maximum cut depth and length, and fill whatever is left. Every cell then drains to the map edge. Breach and fill masks show the changes.

nodes.label: Lake shore
nodes.description: Shape lake shores without changing lake levels: sandy beaches with a Dean equilibrium profile under water and a berm above it, rocky shores with a wave-cut bench and notch, reed shelves in sheltered bays. Fetch (open water upwind) scales the closure depth, berm and bench. Lakes come from FlowRoute, Lakes or Lake, or are found when the input is not connected.

nodes.label: Landform (uplift and rivers)
nodes.description: Grow mountains from an uplift map: rivers cut into rising rock until erosion balances uplift, which forms dendritic valleys, spurs, cols and varying crest heights. Implicit stream power with deposition, lakes that trap sediment and hillslope diffusion, in metres and years. White uplift rises at the given rate; white resistance erodes less.

nodes.label: Lava flows
nodes.description: Lava flows from vents run down the terrain one after another: each follows a wandering steepest descent, fills the valleys it runs in and stops at its length or where the ground flattens, as a flat-topped lobe with steep margins, levees and a rounded snout. Outputs lava thickness and relative flow age for materials.

nodes.label: Normal map
nodes.description: Tangent-space normal map for Unreal materials, packed 0..1 (x east in red, y south in green for DirectX, z up in blue). Measure scale smooths the surface over a Gaussian radius in metres first, so preview and build grids give the same map.

nodes.label: Ambient occlusion
nodes.description: Horizon-based ambient occlusion over a radius in metres: 1 under open sky, darker in pits, valley floors and at the foot of cliffs. Planes are fully open whatever their slope. Sampled at fixed distances in metres, so preview and build grids agree.

nodes.label: Relative height selector
nodes.description: Select by relative height instead of absolute metres, so the selection survives changes upstream. Normalized: position between the robust low and high of this terrain. Height above drainage: metres above the nearest stream. Topographic position: valley (low) to ridge (high) at a neighbourhood radius. The band is in the 0..1 units of the value output.

nodes.label: Rock map
nodes.description: Where bare rock shows: steep faces above the angle where soil holds, and convex crests and edges on steep ground, plus an optional exposed-rock input. Slope and curvature are measured over a scale in metres, so preview and build grids agree.

nodes.label: Rockfall & scree
nodes.description: Rock faces steeper than the release angle shed debris. It runs down the steepest path, stops where the slope eases below the scree angle or its energy line flattens below the run-out angle, and settles into talus cones under gullies and aprons along cliff feet. White resistance keeps rock from releasing (parallel: resistant rock stands up to the resistant release angle and its debris rests at the coarse scree angle); black mask protects cells. Closed edges conserve volume. Resolution independent. Parallel execution moves every column at once (GPU-capable) and settles the fresh debris at its angle of repose.

coarseAngle.label: Scree angle on resistant rock (°, parallel)

nodes.label: Sea and coast
nodes.description: Floods the terrain below a sea level from the map edge and shapes the coast. Exposed rocky shores retreat into wave-cut platforms below cliffs; gentle shores get Dean equilibrium beaches out to the closure depth with a berm above the waterline. Exposure comes from the open-water fetch towards the swell. All lengths are in metres, so the coast keeps its size at every resolution.

levelFraction.label: Share of the map under the sea

openSeaFetch.label: Open sea beyond the map edge (m)

nodes.label: Slope blur
nodes.description: Blur along the downslope direction only. Smooths noise and steps into continuous, flowing slopes while gullies and spurs across the slope stay sharp; crests are protected. Distances are in world metres, so previews and builds match.

nodes.label: Snow
nodes.description: Form-aware snow cover: a snowline in metres or as a fraction of the relief, lower on shaded faces, scoured from wind-exposed ridges and collected in lee slopes and hollows, then redistributed by avalanches so steep faces shed their snow into couloirs and cones. Outputs the snow-covered surface, snow cover, snow depth in metres and avalanche tracks.

snowlineFraction.label: Snowline in the relief (0 lowest, 1 highest)

nodes.label: Soil map
nodes.description: Where soil and sediment lie: gentle slopes, hollows and valley floors, drainage paths and deposition. Slope and curvature are measured over a scale in metres and flow by specific catchment area, so preview and build grids agree. Without a flow input the node routes the terrain itself.

nodes.label: Strata (rock layers)
nodes.description: Layered rock: a dipping, folded stack of beds with an erodibility and a critical slope per layer. Feed resistance into Landform or StreamPower (set their resistance contrast to 1), or connect any output to Plateau (canyonlands) so the layers are re-evaluated as the rock is cut: hard beds stand as cliffs and ledges, soft beds as slopes. Flat beds give mesas and stepped canyons, 5-30 degrees cuestas, steeper hogbacks.

nodes.label: Stream power erosion
nodes.description: Rivers erode the terrain for a duration: implicit stream power with random receivers, deposition that fills valleys and builds fans, lakes that trap sediment as deltas, and hillslope diffusion, in metres and years. Optional uplift and resistance (white resists). Wear and deposit masks are white at a stated thickness.

nodes.label: Upscale detail
nodes.description: Make a coarse simulation or a coarse imported heightfield look detailed at the graph resolution. Re-samples the input at its source spacing, rebuilds a smooth surface through those samples (no bilinear facets or grid), then adds flow-aligned gullies and roughness below twice the source spacing, down to the target spacing. Detail follows slope and curvature and stays off flats, lakes and the ring around small lakes; gullies start only at channel heads.

nodes.label: Valley fill
nodes.description: Fill eroded V valleys with sediment where their drainage area is large: broad flat floodplain floors that widen downstream, rise gently to the valley walls and stop there. Deep closed basins stay lakes at their spill level, small hollows stay as they are, other basins fill with sediment that drains gently towards their outlet. Only raises the terrain.
